title: Hand-feed a pinned seam past the needle, pulling each pin just before it gets there
instruction: Sew the seam: move the cream plate at least 16 cm toward the needle by its black handle only. Grip each red pin and pull it out of the plate while it is beside the yellow bands before the needle, not earlier and not later, and put it in the black dish; never knock a pin loose. No pin may reach the needle or be carried under the needle head, and the plate may move only while a gripper holds its handle. Finish with both grippers open or clear of the handle and the pins.
context: Machine sewing by sewing machine operators, upholsterers, tailors and quilters (O*NET 51-6031.00 Sewing Machine Operators, 51-6093.00 Upholsterers, 51-6052.00 Tailors, Dressmakers, and Custom Sewers). In free-motion quilting, darning or embroidery the feed dogs are dropped and the operator moves the work, often held in a frame or hoop, under a fixed needle. Pins hold the layers in register and are taken out one by one just ahead of the needle: not earlier, or the layers shift; not later, because sewing over a pin can bend or break the needle and throw fragments, as machine manuals and sewing guides commonly warn. Stopping the work to pull a pin is normal practice. For a robot this is a two-sided just-in-time window on work it moves itself: one hand moves the framed work past a fixed needle by its handle, the other pulls each pin in its window, and no pin may reach the needle. Reach splits the two jobs between the arms.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Machine bed: a grey aluminium plate 120 mm (x) by 970 mm (y), 12 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 40.0 cm, y -7.0 cm (from y -55.5 to +41.5 cm). On its top, on the 25 mm strips beside the plate on both sides (centred at x 35.25 and 44.75 cm), painted marks 20 mm wide and 1 mm thick: a red one 6 mm long on the needle line (y -36.0 cm) and a yellow band over the pull window, from y -33.0 to -29.0 cm (30 to 70 mm before the needle line). (2) Frame plate: cream PVC foam board standing in for two plies of a pinned seam held in a sliding frame, 70 mm (x) by 760 mm (y), 10 mm thick, lying on the bed along its centre line (x 36.5 to 43.5 cm, y -35.5 to +40.5 cm at the start, its top 22 mm above the table). It slides on a rail toward -y (to the right) only, up to 180 mm, with light damping (2 N s per m) and no spring; it moves only when pushed or pulled; 0.30 kg with its handle. A blue seam line 3 mm wide runs down its centre (x 40.0 cm). Three square pockets, 28 x 28 mm and 6 mm deep, are cut on the seam line at y -30.5, -25.5 and -20.5 cm. A handle, a black plastic block 30 x 30 x 40 mm, is fixed on the plate centred at x 40.0 cm, y +38.0 cm. (3) to (5) Pins 1 to 3: loose aluminium cylinders painted red, standing in for pin heads, 18 mm across and 40 mm tall, 27 g each, standing upright in the pockets (pin 1 at y -30.5 cm, 55 mm before the needle line, inside the window; pin 2 at -25.5 cm; pin 3 at -20.5 cm), their bottoms 16 mm above the table. (6) Needle head: a fixed bridge of grey painted steel over the bed, just beyond the needle line: two posts 10 x 10 mm, 75 mm tall, standing on the table 2 mm outside the bed's sides (centred at x 33.3 and 46.7 cm, y -36.5 cm), a cross bar 144 x 10 x 15 mm on them (75 to 90 mm above the table, y -37.0 to -36.0 cm), and a steel needle, a 4 mm rod, hanging from the bar's near edge on the needle line (x 40.0 cm, y -36.0 cm) down to 30 mm above the table, 8 mm above the plate. A pin riding in the plate cannot pass under it. (7) Pin dish: a fixed open tray of black plastic, 140 x 70 mm inside (140 mm along x), 6 mm walls 15 mm tall, 4 mm floor, centred at x 24.0 cm, y -40.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table. With the gripper straight down or tilted up to 40 degrees, only the left arm reaches the handle at the start and only the right arm reaches the pull window and the dish.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the plate's travel along its rail (the feed), the three pins and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's finger-tip point (between the tips) and opening (0 closed, 1 open with the fingers 94 mm apart). A pin's d is its centre's distance before the needle line along the seam. A pin is in the plate while its centre is over the plate and its lowest point less than 3 mm above the plate's top (standing in its pocket it is 6 mm below the top). A gripper holds a pin when its opening is under 0.30 (fingers under 28 mm apart) and its finger-tip point is within 4 mm of the pin. A pin is pulled when it leaves the plate (lifted out of its pocket or slid off the plate's side) while a gripper holds it; only its first pull counts. It is pulled in time if d was then 30 to 70 mm (the yellow bands) and it never came closer than 30 mm to the needle line while in the plate, at any time in the trial. A gripper holds the handle when its opening is under 0.6 and its finger-tip point is over the handle's footprint grown by 5 mm and below the handle's top. A pin is in the dish when its centre is over the dish's floor, its lowest point below the rim, and it is still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). A gripper has let go when its opening is 0.9 or more or its finger-tip point is more than 20 mm from the handle and every pin. Fed means the furthest the plate has slid along its rail. Score 0, whatever happens afterwards, if at any moment: any part of a pin comes within 6 mm of the needle line or crosses it (an upright pin's centre within 15 mm) while the pin's centre is between the needle head's posts (within 72 mm of the seam line) and its lowest point below the bar's top (90 mm above the table), so a pin riding into the needle and a pin carried past it under the bar both count; a pin leaves the plate while no gripper holds it (knocked loose: a loose pin on a machine bed can be fed under the foot or into the bobbin); the plate moves more than 5 mm in all while no gripper holds its handle; or a pin falls off the table (its lowest point 10 mm or more below the table's top). Otherwise: 1.0 if the plate has been fed 160 mm or more (past where pin 3 started), all three pins were pulled in time, all three are in the dish and both grippers have let go; 0.75 if fed 160 mm with all three pulled in time; 0.5 if two pins were pulled in time; 0.25 if one was and the plate was fed 45 mm or more (pin 1 starts 55 mm before the needle line and is struck once the plate is fed past 40 mm); 0 otherwise. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with the pins still and the plate still (under 5 mm/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, the rules about holding and letting go are taken as met. In a real trial, film from above and from the side: read the feed and each pin's d where it leaves the plate on a ruler along the bed's near edge, and check from the side that each pin is gripped as it leaves and none passes under the needle head.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction. The plies are one rigid plate in a frame on a damped rail, so the window's lower bound stands for keeping the layers in register rather than being simulated. The needle is fixed and does not stitch: reaching it is judged geometrically and physically blocks a riding pin. The pins are scaled-up upright pin heads (18 x 40 mm cylinders standing in pockets) so a gripper can hold them; real pins lie across the seam and slide out sideways.
reset_notes: Slide the plate back to the start of its rail (handle centred at y +38.0 cm), stand the three pins upright in their pockets (pin 1 nearest the needle), and empty the dish. Nothing is consumed or changed by a trial; a real needle that was struck would need replacing, which is why a strike scores 0.
